newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf changes agency, image in new campaign.
newsitem.headline: Elf changes agency, image in new campaign.

text.p: French oil, chemicals and healthcare company Elf Aquitaine said on Friday it was launching a press advertising campaign on Monday which seeks to give a human face to the firm, usually identified with the petrol pump.
The campaign, for a budget of 30 million francs, was won by advertising agency BDDP in competition with FCB, Euro RSCG, BETC and Publicis, an Elf spokeswoman said.
She was confirming a report in the daily newspaper Le Figaro on Friday, which said Elf's new campaign aimed to show its involvement in current problems.

Elf, for which BDDP devised its most recent television spots, using cute animals to claim cleanliness for its diesel and engine oil, has not pushed its corporate image since it was privatised in 1994, the spokeswoman said.

It is running four different adverts, each carrying the slogan, "Elf - human energy", in French national and regional newspapers and in magazines, starting on Monday and running until the summer holidays in July, she said.
The campaign will then resume in the autumn, and at some point Elf plans to run it outside France, she added.
"You don't see the human side very easily with us," she said.
The campaign aims to give Elf a human face using a thought-provoking picture and a question, to which Elf says it has a business that is working on the answer.
The poster illustrating Elf's healthcare business shows an elderly gentleman in sports gear suspended between two acrobats' ropes. "What if you could be as fit at 90 as at 20?" it asks.
Others illustrate environmental protection, oil exploration and the hole in the ozone layer, the Elf spokeswoman said.
She said Elf's studies showed that people reacted to Elf through the thing they knew best, its service stations. The company was keen to show it has other sides, she said.
